To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MAO-B inhibition reduces 18F‐THK5351 binding in the human brain and that this reduction is most pronounced in regions with high baseline 18F‐ THK5351 retention.

the MAO-B inhibitor selegiline reduced 18F‐THK5351 accumulation in the brains of healthy controls and patients with Alzheimer’s disease and mild cognitive impairment, indicating that 18F‐ THK5351 uptake reflects MAO‐B availability, and not tau.

selegiline, an MAO-B inhibitor, significantly reduced 18F-Tau PET signal in the brain of patients with neurodegenerative diseases. 18F-THKS351 PET signal is reduced in patients with neurodegeneration following MAO-B inhibitor administration.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and evaluation of a new radiotracer, 11C-PI-2620, for the detection of tau pathology in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). 11C- PI-2620 is a quinazolinone derivative that was designed based on the structure-activity relationship of the previously developed 11C-THK5355, a tau PET tracer with high binding affinity for the pathological tau aggregates.
the effects of MAOB inhibition on 18 F-THK535 PET images.
the development of a new imaging technique to detect and quantify the presence of the tau protein in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
18F- THK5351 uptake is a combination of tau binding and MAO-B binding.
the 18F- THK5351 uptake is confounded by MAO-B availability and thus the 18F-T HK5351 uptake cannot be used to assess PHF in the human brain.
the interpretation of PET scans with 18F- THK5351 is currently confounded by the presence of MAO-B in the brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 18F-FLUTET-MCAO-B PET imaging is not recommended for clinical use.
18F- THK5351 is not an appropriate tau PET tracer for human studies.
18F-FLORbetapir and 18F-AV-1451 may be more appropriate tau PET tracers for the study of tau in vivo, given the lack of MAO-B binding in the human brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 18F-TRH5351 signal should be interpreted with caution.
the use of a MAO-B inhibitor, such as selegiline, should be avoided prior to a 18F- THK5351 PET scan.
18F-THR5351 is not an optimal tau imaging agent.
